title: Loaded
description: What the settings file or program gives.

gap.description: Between panes and around them, in px

always_frame.description: Border, gap and radius also on a pane alone in its tree, and on the treeview

opacity.description:
Of Sonamu's own translucent backgrounds and treeview (applets, panels, rows), so what's behind shows through:
1 is opaque. Menus and popups are always opaque

wallpaper.description: Drawn behind everything, even wallpaper programs' layers (#104); on battery, `battery_wallpaper` if set

battery_wallpaper.description: The wallpaper while on battery (eg a still image instead of a shader): `same` is `wallpaper`

font_size.description: Text height in px (Sonamu's own UI isn't scaled)

mipmaps.description:
Smaller copies of windows and images, so they look smooth when drawn small (eg the zoom-out view); a bit
more GPU work each time a window updates

buffer_line.description: When the buffer line (a prompt at the bottom, like vim's command line: the agent, `!` Luau, `$` shell) shows

agent_url.description:
The buffer line's agent: an OpenAI-compatible server (eg llama.cpp's `llama-server` at
`http://127.0.0.1:8080`); `None`: no agent

notifications.description: Desktop notifications, shown by the status bar (#150)

keybinds.description:
Global shortcuts in named groups (shown as help sections): Sonamu commands or shell commands. Given, it
replaces the defaults (list the groups to keep)

restore_programs.description: Programs restored running in their terminal (see `.claude/SESSIONS.md`)

startup.description: Shell commands run once when Sonamu starts (eg `dms run`)

terminal.description: Program started by Super+T; `None`: `$TERMINAL`, else the first installed of a list

browser.description: Program started by Super+N; `None`: `$BROWSER`, else the first installed of a list

pdf_viewer.description: Program the file manager opens PDFs in; `None`: the first installed of zathura, okular, evince

watch.description: Extra files to watch for changes, eg the ones the program reads.

bg.description:
The command hub's, buffer line's and help's background (translucent; their bars a bit toward `fg`). Not behind the
panes: the background layer (eg a wallpaper) is there

fg.description: Text of the treeview and projects

accent.description: Focus on a node itself (traversal keys move it): its border and treeview marker

inactive.description: Text of inactive (eg hibernated) nodes in the treeview

focused.description: Focus is inside the pane's applet (keys go to it); also its treeview marker

oneOf.description: Nothing: what's under shows (eg a wallpaper program's layer, else black)
An image file (`~` or relative to the config dir), covering each screen

A Shadertoy-style fragment shader, reloaded when the file changes. GLSL: `void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor,
in vec2 fragCoord)` with `iTime`, `iResolution`, `iFrame`, `iMouse`. A `.wgsl` file: `fn main_image(position: vec2f)
-> vec4f` with `wallpaper.time`, `.resolution`, `.frame` (`u32`), `.mouse`; it may declare `wallpaper` itself
(`struct Wallpaper { resolution: vec2f, time: f32, frame: u32, mouse: vec4f }` at group 0, binding 0)

path.description: The shader file (`~` or relative to the config dir)

scale.description: Drawn at this fraction of the screen's resolution and stretched: lower is cheaper

fps.description: Frames per second it's drawn at

oneOf.description: Nothing: what's under shows (eg a wallpaper program's layer, else black)
An image file (`~` or relative to the config dir), covering each screen

A Shadertoy-style fragment shader, reloaded when the file changes. GLSL: `void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor,
in vec2 fragCoord)` with `iTime`, `iResolution`, `iFrame`, `iMouse`. A `.wgsl` file: `fn main_image(position: vec2f)
-> vec4f` with `wallpaper.time`, `.resolution`, `.frame` (`u32`), `.mouse`; it may declare `wallpaper` itself
(`struct Wallpaper { resolution: vec2f, time: f32, frame: u32, mouse: vec4f }` at group 0, binding 0)

TreeviewSettings.description: Whether the treeview is pinned is part of the session, toggled by its pin button

side.description: The side a pinned one is on

width.description: The side column's width, in percent of the window's

floating.description: Where an unpinned one floats (only while focus is on a node)

floating_size.description: A `Center` floating one's width and height, in percent of the window's

TreeviewSide.description: A column beside the panes, which get the rest of the width

TreeviewFloating.description: Where an unpinned treeview floats over the panes, which keep their size

oneOf.description: Only in buffer mode (Super+Esc), over the panes
Always, below the panes; `INSERT` while not in buffer mode

SwipeSettings.description: 3 finger touchpad swipes between nodes (#141): left / right between siblings, up / down between parent and child (#144)

distance_x.description: How far the fingers move left / right to go one node, in px

distance_y.description: How far the fingers move up / down to go one node, in px

rubber_band.description: How far past the first / last node it stretches at most, in nodes

stiffness.description: Of the spring settling on a node after the fingers lift (mass 1): higher is faster

damping_ratio.description: Of that spring: 1 is critically damped (no bounce), below 1 overshoots and bounces, above 1 is sluggish

ZoomOutSettings.description: The zoom-out view (#145); pinches scale it

child_previews.description: Tiny previews of the children of the nodes beside each row's own, under their panes

view.description: Whether the view floats freely (default), or keeps its center in the middle

oneOf.description: It pans to keep its center (where clicks, arrows and 2 finger scrolls move it) in the middle
2 finger scrolls move it freely; clicks and arrows still move its center, but it stays put

timeout.description: How long a new one pops up, in seconds (unless it asks for its own time; critical ones stay)

Keybind.description: Does `action` when `key` is pressed with exactly `mods` held

Key.description: A character (case-insensitive), a key's name, or an evdev code for other keys (eg 115 is volume up)

RestoreProgram.description:
A program (matched by its name) restored running in its terminal: with its saved args,
or with these instead (eg `claude` with `--continue`)
